1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# Renders hack/build-job.yaml and runs it in the target cluster.
3	#
4	# Called from `make build BUILD_TARGET=<sun|nukedev|nukeprod|kubectl-context>`
5	# (Makefile.docker) with
6	# BUILD_TARGET, NAMESPACE, REPO_URL, REF, TAG, DOCKERFILE, IMAGE, PUSH,
7	# PUSH_SECRET and TIMEOUT in the environment. Not intended to be run by hand.
8	set -euo pipefail
9	
10	SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
11	TEMPLATE="${TEMPLATE:-${SCRIPT_DIR}/build-job.yaml}"
12	
13	NAMESPACE="${NAMESPACE:-build}"
14	PUSH="${PUSH:-true}"
15	TIMEOUT="${TIMEOUT:-3600}"
16	DOCKERFILE="${DOCKERFILE:-Dockerfile}"
17	DOCKER_REGISTRY="${DOCKER_REGISTRY:-docker.io}"
18	
19	die() {
20		echo "build-cluster: $*" >&2
21		exit 1
22	}
23	
24	require() {
25		local name="$1"
26		[ -n "${!name:-}" ] || die "${name} is required; pass it on the make command line"
27	}
28	
29	# BUILD_TARGET is resolved to a kubeconfig file and context by cluster-alias.sh,
30	# which also defines the kc() helper every kubectl call goes through.
31	source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/cluster-alias.sh"
32	
33	# The equivalent invocation for messages the operator has to retype.
34	KUBE_HINT="kubectl --context ${KUBE_CONTEXT}"
35	[ -z "${KUBECONFIG_PATH}" ] || KUBE_HINT="KUBECONFIG=${KUBECONFIG_PATH} ${KUBE_HINT}"
36	
37	require BUILD_TARGET
38	require REPO_URL
39	require REF
40	require TAG
41	require IMAGE
42	require PUSH_SECRET
43	
44	# Values are substituted into the manifest with sed and land in shell scripts
45	# inside it, so each one is restricted to a whitelist before rendering. A value
46	# outside the whitelist is rejected, never escaped.
47	printf '%s' "${REF}" | grep -qE '^[A-Za-z0-9._/-]+$' ||
48		die "REF '${REF}' contains characters outside [A-Za-z0-9._/-]"
49	printf '%s' "${TAG}" | grep -qE '^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$' ||
50		die "TAG '${TAG}' contains characters outside [A-Za-z0-9._-]"
51	printf '%s' "${IMAGE}" | grep -qE '^[A-Za-z0-9._/:-]+$' ||
52		die "IMAGE '${IMAGE}' contains characters outside [A-Za-z0-9._/:-]"
53	printf '%s' "${REPO_URL}" | grep -qE '^[A-Za-z0-9._/:@-]+$' ||
54		die "REPO_URL '${REPO_URL}' contains characters outside [A-Za-z0-9._/:@-]"
55	printf '%s' "${DOCKERFILE}" | grep -qE '^[A-Za-z0-9._/-]+$' ||
56		die "DOCKERFILE '${DOCKERFILE}' contains characters outside [A-Za-z0-9._/-]"
57	printf '%s' "${PUSH_SECRET}" | grep -qE '^[a-z0-9]([-a-z0-9.]*[a-z0-9])?$' ||
58		die "PUSH_SECRET '${PUSH_SECRET}' is not a valid Kubernetes secret name"
59	printf '%s' "${DOCKER_REGISTRY}" | grep -qE '^[A-Za-z0-9._/:-]+$' ||
60		die "DOCKER_REGISTRY '${DOCKER_REGISTRY}' contains characters outside [A-Za-z0-9._/:-]"
61	printf '%s' "${TIMEOUT}" | grep -qE '^[0-9]+$' ||
62		die "TIMEOUT '${TIMEOUT}' is not a number of seconds"
63	printf '%s' "${NAMESPACE}" | grep -qE '^[a-z0-9]([-a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9])?$' ||
64		die "NAMESPACE '${NAMESPACE}' is not a valid Kubernetes namespace name"
65	case "${PUSH}" in
66	true | false) ;;
67	*) die "PUSH '${PUSH}' must be true or false" ;;
68	esac
69	
70	# `grep -qE '^...$'` matches when ANY line matches, so a value carrying a newline
71	# passes the whitelist on its first line and its remaining lines are injected
72	# verbatim by sed into the YAML and the embedded `sh -c` script. Reject embedded
73	# newlines for every value before rendering.
74	for _var in REF TAG IMAGE REPO_URL DOCKERFILE PUSH_SECRET DOCKER_REGISTRY TIMEOUT NAMESPACE; do
75		case "${!_var}" in
76		*$'\n'*) die "${_var} contains a newline, which is not allowed" ;;
77		esac
78	done
79	
80	if [ -n "${KUBECONFIG_PATH}" ] && [ ! -f "${KUBECONFIG_PATH}" ]; then
81		die "BUILD_TARGET '${BUILD_TARGET}' needs the kubeconfig ${KUBECONFIG_PATH}, which does not exist"
82	fi
83	
84	# The accepted targets are the contexts the resolved kubeconfig knows about, so
85	# an unknown target fails here with the list instead of at apply time. The
86	# aliases are listed too: they are valid inputs without being contexts.
87	contexts="$(kc config get-contexts -o name 2>/dev/null || true)"
88	printf '%s\n' "${contexts}" | grep -qxF "${KUBE_CONTEXT}" ||
89		die "unknown BUILD_TARGET '${BUILD_TARGET}'; accepted values: sun nukedev nukeprod $(printf '%s' "${contexts}" | tr '\n' ' ')"
90	
91	# The build clock is the built commit's timestamp. It is rendered literally so
92	# the Job states the epoch it will use; the init container re-derives it from
93	# the cloned commit and the build container refuses to run on a mismatch.
94	if [ -z "${SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH:-}" ]; then
95		SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH="$(git log -1 --format=%ct "${REF}" 2>/dev/null || true)"
96	fi
97	printf '%s' "${SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH}" | grep -qE '^[0-9]+$' ||
98		die "cannot resolve REF '${REF}' to a commit in the local repository; run git fetch and retry"
99	# SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH is the one substituted value the loop above cannot cover: it

2	# Resolves BUILD_TARGET into the kubeconfig file and kubectl context that
3	# `kubectl` actually needs, and provides the kc() helper every call goes
4	# through. Sourced by hack/build-cluster.sh; keeping the mapping here rather
5	# than inline means any future caller shares it instead of restating it.
6	#
7	# Defines variables and a function only: no `set -euo pipefail`, no `exit`,
8	# no output. The sourcing script owns all of that.
9	
10	# BUILD_TARGET is either a kubectl context in the default kubeconfig or one of
11	# the build clusters, whose contexts live in their own kubeconfig files under a
12	# name that differs from the one people use for the cluster. Resolve the alias
13	# into the kubeconfig file and context that kubectl actually needs; anything
14	# that is not an alias stays a plain context name. A case statement, not an
15	# associative array: macOS still ships bash 3.2.
16	KUBECONFIG_PATH=""
17	KUBE_CONTEXT="${BUILD_TARGET:-}"
18	case "${BUILD_TARGET:-}" in
19	sun)
20		KUBECONFIG_PATH="${HOME}/.kube/sun"
21		KUBE_CONTEXT=default
22		;;
23	nukedev)
24		KUBECONFIG_PATH="${HOME}/.kube/nuke-dev"
25		KUBE_CONTEXT=nuke-dev
26		;;
27	nukeprod)
28		KUBECONFIG_PATH="${HOME}/.kube/nuke-prod"
29		KUBE_CONTEXT=nuke-prod
30		;;
31	esac
32	
33	# Every kubectl call goes through this, so the resolved kubeconfig and context
34	# cannot drift between the validation and the calls it guards.
35	kc() {

37			KUBECONFIG="${KUBECONFIG_PATH}" kubectl --context "${KUBE_CONTEXT}" "$@"
38		else
39			kubectl --context "${KUBE_CONTEXT}" "$@"
40		fi

111	11. `make precommit` and `make test` exist and are container-safe: `precommit` runs `bash -n` over the three `hack/` scripts and `make -n build`, and neither target invokes `docker`. Both land in a bootstrap commit before any prompt runs — the pipeline's preflight executes `make precommit` before the prompt container starts, so a prompt that creates them is too late.
112	
113	## Constraints
114	
115	- The local recipe's `docker build` arguments must not change: `--no-cache --rm=true --platform=linux/amd64 -t $(REGISTRY)/$(IMAGE):$(VERSION) .` stays, and no build args are added.
116	- `VERSION`, `REGISTRY` and `IMAGE` keep their current definitions and meanings. `VERSION` remains the image tag and keeps its `?= 1.3.0` default on line 1.
117	- **The defaulted-`VERSION` guard must sit inside the cluster branch only.** `VERSION` is assigned in the file itself, so `$(origin VERSION)` reads `file` on every bare `make build`; a guard evaluated at parse time would refuse the local arm, which is the opposite of the intent. The copied `ALLOW_DEFAULT_VERSION` bypass is deliberately not carried over (see Non-goals).
118	- `hack/build-job.yaml` must not live under a `k8s/` directory — a directory-scanned `make apply` would adopt it as deploy state. This repository has no `k8s/` directory today and must not gain one for this file.
119	- The Job image is referenced by digest, not by a floating tag.
120	- No new runtime dependency in the built image. This change is build tooling only.
121	- The local path must work with no kubeconfig and no cluster credentials present.
122	- `docs/dod.md`'s "`make build` succeeds" is a host-side check: the dark-factory container has no Docker daemon, so a prompt must not treat its inability to run `docker build` as a failure. `make -n build` and the `bash -n` checks are the container-executable substitutes.
123	- **`make precommit` and `make test` are the pipeline's gates and both land in a bootstrap commit before any prompt runs.** `.dark-factory.yaml` leaves `validationCommand: make precommit` and `testCommand: make test` at their dark-factory defaults, and preflight executes `make precommit` *before* the prompt container starts. Both targets are therefore added up front and must stay Docker-free, since the container has no daemon.
124	- **No Go-specific plugin documentation.** This repo ships a `Dockerfile` and build scripts, not Go code. Prompts must not cite `coding/docs/go-makefile-commands.md` or any other language-specific plugin doc, and `make test` is intentionally a no-op rather than a test suite.
125	- The five `hack/` files are copied from the pinned refs with their comments and hardening intact; the repository-specific values (image, repo URL) come from the Makefile environment, not from edits to the scripts. One inherited comment in `build-job.yaml` refers to a release-to-image dispatcher this repo does not have — that inaccuracy is accepted rather than edited, to keep the copy byte-faithful.
126	- **Reference**: the canonical procedure is `bborbe/go-skeleton` `docs/build-migration-guide.md` at `eb050aa20bb6194d8af7e47baf8880df789bd1ca`. This repo deliberately diverges in two places — the local arm stays plain `docker build` (the guide mandates `buildx` with `rewrite-timestamp`), and `VERSION` keeps `?= 1.3.0` (the guide has no default). A prompt must not "correct" either divergence.
127	
128	## Failure Modes
129	
130	| Trigger | Expected behavior | Recovery |
131	|---|---|---|
132	| `BUILD_TARGET` names a cluster alias with no kubeconfig file | `build-cluster.sh` exits non-zero naming the missing file; no Job is created | Provision the kubeconfig, or use `sun` / `nukedev` / `nukeprod` |
133	| `BUILD_TARGET` names an unknown target | `build-cluster.sh` dies at its context check with `unknown BUILD_TARGET '<x>'; accepted values: sun nukedev nukeprod <contexts>`; no cluster call is made and no Job is created | Rerun with `sun`, `nukedev` or `nukeprod` |
134	| The cluster is unreachable | `build-cluster.sh` exits non-zero at the existence probe, carrying kubectl's connection error; no partial Job is left | Rerun when the cluster is available; `kubectl<wrapper> get ns build` confirms it |
135	| The Job is rejected at admission (pod-security, RBAC) | The make target prints the Job's events and exits non-zero | `kubectl<wrapper> -n build describe job build-<TAG>` shows no `FailedCreate` after the fix |
136	| The `build` namespace or `buildkit-push` secret is missing | The Job is created but its pod cannot mount the secret and never starts | Run `hack/build-cluster-bootstrap.sh <cluster>` once, then rerun the build |
137	| The git clone fails in the init container | The Job fails; its log names the ref and the git error | Correct `REF`, or verify the ref exists on the remote |
138	| The cluster resolves `REF` to a different commit than the local repository | The build container refuses before building: `REF <ref> is commit epoch <x> in the cluster but <y> in the local repository` | Run `git fetch` locally and rerun |
139	| The registry throttles the push | The Job fails at the push with a `429` in its log | Wait and rerun; the Job is idempotent per tag |
140	| The registry push is refused | The Job fails at the push; its log carries the registry error | Verify the mounted secret and its `items:` remap, then rerun |
141	| A Job with the same name already exists | `build-cluster.sh` refuses before applying and names the delete command | Delete the old Job, or use a different `VERSION` |
142	| The Job exceeds its deadline | The make target fails and names the deadline it waited | Raise `BUILD_TIMEOUT`, or investigate why the build stalled |
143	| The build node cannot schedule the pod (request capacity) | The pod stays `Pending` and the Job hits its deadline; the make target exits non-zero | `kubectl<wrapper> -n build describe pod -l job-name=build-<TAG>` shows the scheduling event; free capacity or lower the request |
144	| `make build` is interrupted mid-wait | The Job continues in the cluster; a later `kubectl<wrapper> get job build-<TAG>` reports its state | Read the Job's state, or delete it explicitly |
145	
146	## Security / Abuse
147	
148	- The push credential exists only as a cluster secret, mounted into the build pod. It is never written to the invoking machine, never passed as a make variable, and never printed.
149	- `hack/build-cluster.sh` whitelists every value it substitutes into the manifest and rejects embedded newlines before rendering, so a crafted `REF`, `TAG` or `IMAGE` cannot inject YAML or shell.
150	- The `items:` remap is load-bearing: without it the secret file keeps its own name while Docker looks for `config.json`, and auth fails in the same shape a missing credential produces.
151	- `buildctl-daemonless.sh` runs rootless with `--oci-worker-no-process-sandbox`. No privileged pod, no host namespace, no Docker socket.
152	- The init container sets `automountServiceAccountToken: false` and drops all capabilities; the build container carries no cluster credentials and cannot create, read or modify other resources.
153	- `REF` is passed as a clone argument, not interpolated into a shell string, so a crafted ref cannot execute commands in the init container.
154	
155	## Suggested Decomposition
156	
157	| # | Prompt focus | Covers DBs | Covers ACs | Depends on |
158	|---|---|---|---|---|
159	| 1 | Copy `hack/build-cluster.sh` and `hack/cluster-alias.sh` verbatim from `agent-task-executor@91a7e64` (bodies inlined into the prompt) | 5, 6 | 7 | — |
160	| 2 | Copy `hack/build-job.yaml` from `agent-task-executor@91a7e64` and `hack/build-cluster-bootstrap.sh` + `hack/dockerconfig.json.tpl` from `go-skeleton@eb050aa` (bodies inlined) | 5, 6, 7 | 7 | — |
161	| 3 | `BUILD_TARGET` selector, local-arm freeze, defaulted-`VERSION` guard | 1, 4, 8 | 1, 2, 3 | prompts 1–2 |
162	| 4 | Cluster branch wiring: render, apply, wait, report; Job naming | 2, 3, 9 | 4, 5, 6 | prompt 3 |
163	| 5 | `upload` / `clean` no-ops and the `## Unreleased` entry | 10 | 8, 9 | prompt 3 |
164	
165	Rationale: prompts 1 and 2 are verbatim copies of static files with no behaviour change and are independently verifiable; prompt 3 edits only the local arm and the guard and is independently testable with `make -n`; prompt 4 is the only prompt that shells out to a cluster; prompt 5 is small and orthogonal. **DB11 / AC10 (`precommit`, `test`) are already satisfied by a bootstrap commit** — the pipeline's preflight runs `make precommit` before any prompt container starts, so they cannot be created by a prompt. The operator-executable rung runs after merge, so no prompt depends on a cluster being reachable.
166	
167	**How prompts 1 and 2 obtain the bodies.** The prompt-creator runs on the host, not in the container. It reads each file at generation time with `git -C ~/Documents/workspaces/agent-task-executor show 91a7e64e160f30be8af0aea64635e1e11bc86731:hack/<file>` (and `git -C ~/Documents/workspaces/go-skeleton show eb050aa20bb6194d8af7e47baf8880df789bd1ca:hack/<file>` for `build-cluster-bootstrap.sh` and `dockerconfig.json.tpl`) and inlines the content into the prompt body. The executing container must never be asked to reach either repository. If generation is ever containerised, the fallback is to land the five bodies under `docs/` in this repo first and have the prompt copy from there.
168	
169	## Do-Nothing Option
170	
171	`openldap`'s image keeps requiring this Mac. The repo stays in the un-migrated half of the build-cluster rollout, the goal's per-repo evidence row cannot be written, and the release path keeps its single point of failure. The mirror and the StatefulSet keep pulling an image that can only be cut by hand on one machine.
